decision: Use a pnpm monorepo with packages/engine, adapters, themes, renderer-pixi, audio and apps/web
rationale: Package boundaries make the engine/UI decoupling visible and lint-enforceable for provider reviewers
tradeoffs: More workspace/tooling setup than a single Vite app

decision: Render reels with PixiJS v8 (see ADR-0002)
rationale: Industry-standard WebGL renderer for slot studios; GPU batching, filters and HiDPI out of the box
tradeoffs: ~200KB gzipped dependency; WebGL context-loss handling is our responsibility

decision: Pure engine package with ports (OutcomeProvider, ReelsPort, Clock, Rng); React only in apps/web (ADR-0001)
rationale: Deterministic, Node-testable game logic; renderer/UI/backend are swappable
tradeoffs: Port contracts must be designed up front; slight indirection from click to reel

decision: Table-driven reducer with effect descriptors, spinId stale-response guard, rejected events recorded not thrown (ADR-0003)
rationale: Makes double-spins and stale responses impossible and every transition inspectable
tradeoffs: Adding states requires table + test updates

decision: Server-authoritative OutcomeProvider port returning a discriminated union; MockProvider with latency/error injection and forced scenarios (ADR-0004)
rationale: Client code mirrors production against a real RGS; QA can force edge cases deterministically
tradeoffs: Mock 'server' logic ships in the demo bundle

decision: Single validated GameConfig drives layout, maths, paytable and theme tokens (ADR-0005)
rationale: New titles become data; paytable can never drift from maths
tradeoffs: Exotic mechanics need future engine extension points

decision: Ban enum/interface via ESLint no-restricted-syntax; money as integer minor units; even integer line-heights
rationale: Explicit union types and as-const objects are tree-shakeable and erase cleanly; integer cents avoid float drift
tradeoffs: Slightly more verbose type declarations

decision: Tune paytables by Monte-Carlo to ~95% RTP (neon-relic 95.1%, crystal-ways 94.5%) and gate configs in CI with simulate() bounds 85-105%
rationale: Unbalanced demo maths (51%/147%) would make the demo feel broken; a CI sim catches config regressions
tradeoffs: Estimated RTP only (40k spins, ±~2%); not a certified maths model

decision: Client-side request timeout (8s) synthesises a TIMEOUT error; late responses are rejected by state/spinId guards; balance resynced via provider.getBalance() on RECOVER
rationale: Prevents a hung request from wedging the round and keeps the displayed balance authoritative after errors
tradeoffs: Server may have settled a timed-out spin; we rely on balance resync rather than round replay

decision: Slam-stop is context-aware: queued in SPIN_REQUESTED, quick-stop in SPINNING, skip in STOPPING, skip presentation in WIN_PRESENTATION; spin button stops autoplay first
rationale: Matches player expectations across providers; one input never causes two state changes
tradeoffs: Players must press twice to both stop autoplay and slam the current spin

decision: Engine tsconfig targets ES2022 without DOM lib; timers reached through a typed globalThis host in clock.ts only
rationale: Compiler-level proof that the engine has no DOM dependency, beyond the lint rule
tradeoffs: Small typed shim for setTimeout/performance

decision: Reel = virtual unbounded strip (Map index→id) rendered through rows+2 pooled sprites; stop target planned >= rows+1 symbols ahead so outcome symbols never pop into view
rationale: No per-frame allocation; outcome injection is invisible; motion is a pure function in reel-math.ts tested across 4-50ms frame times
tradeoffs: No fixed reel strips: filler symbols are visual only (server outcome is authoritative)

decision: Velocity-continuous decel (v0 = power*distance/duration) + overshoot/settle; motion blur filter attached only above 15% speed; static frame/glow layer cacheAsTexture; particles pooled (160)
rationale: Smooth 60fps on mid devices: no filter cost at rest, no GC during big wins
tradeoffs: Blur quality kept at 2 passes; cacheAsTexture must be refreshed on every layout

decision: Synthesize all SFX with Web Audio oscillators/noise; lazy AudioContext on first gesture; every call try/catch no-op; prefs in guarded localStorage; audio observes controller events via bindAudio
rationale: Zero asset loading failures, autoplay-policy safe, and audio can never wedge or crash the game loop
tradeoffs: Synth SFX are less rich than produced audio; swap in decoded buffers later behind the same Sfx ids

decision: Ignore webglcontextlost after destroy(); raise motion delta cap from 50ms to 100ms
rationale: StrictMode remount destroys the first Pixi app, which deliberately loses its context and was surfacing a false 'context lost' banner; a 100ms cap keeps real-time pacing down to 10fps devices
tradeoffs: Very long frames (>100ms) still slow game time slightly, by design, to bound jumps after tab switches

decision: Engine created once outside React (main.tsx) and provided via context; UI reads via useSyncExternalStore; ReelCanvas attaches ReelStage as the controller's ReelsPort
rationale: StrictMode double-mounting cannot duplicate the engine; renders only on state changes, never per frame
tradeoffs: Composition root is a module singleton; tests that need isolation call createGame() directly

decision: Responsive HUD: 4-column desktop bar; portrait 2x2 grid with thumb-reach spin bottom-right; phone-landscape right-hand HUD column; app grid column minmax(0,1fr) so HUD min-content never widens the page
rationale: Ergonomic primary action placement per orientation; verified no overlap/overflow at 320-1280px via e2e/layout.mjs
tradeoffs: Extra media-query branches for <=360px phones

decision: Non-modal Provider Inspector (backtick) with live state chain, transition log (rejections highlighted, JSON export), FPS/p95 sparkline polled at 4Hz, config switcher (IDLE-only), mock latency/error/seed/forced-outcome controls and in-browser RTP simulation
rationale: Lets provider reviewers and QA see determinism, guards and perf live while playing
tradeoffs: Inspector ships in the production bundle; gate behind a build flag for real operators

decision: Add puppeteer-core e2e smoke (25 checks) and responsive layout check, run against a live dev server with hardware GPU flags (E2E_GPU=0 falls back to SwiftShader and skips the FPS assertion)
rationale: Proves the whole stack (engine + Pixi + React) in a real browser; headless SwiftShader renders at ~5fps so GPU is required for perf assertions
tradeoffs: Needs a local Chrome and a running dev server; not yet wired into CI

decision: Dev server binds to localhost only; LAN exposure is opt-in via pnpm dev -- --host
rationale: host:true exposed the dev server on all interfaces by default
tradeoffs: Device testing needs the explicit flag
